profile.reading:
Switch Las Vegas 11 sits at 7380 Lindell Road, Las Vegas, Nevada, on Switch's Core Campus in unincorporated Clark County, directly adjacent to Las Vegas 10. Switch's own June 2017 press release for Las Vegas 10's opening notes that construction had already been underway on Las Vegas 10 and Las Vegas 11 together, describing the pair as adding roughly 700,000 combined square feet to the Core Campus; Switch has not published an individual square footage or megawatt figure specifically isolated to Las Vegas 11 beyond that combined figure. This building's address is independently corroborated by both this record's OpenStreetMap tagging and two separate third-party data center aggregator directories, giving higher confidence in the address than for some other Core Campus buildings lacking that cross-source agreement. Switch's Core Campus overall is marketed today as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion and 100 percent renewable energy. Switch's Nevada tax-advantages materials describe a consumer-use-tax abatement to as low as 2 percent and a 75 percent property-tax abatement on customer equipment at Switch facilities, administered through Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development. Switch does not name a specific power utility on its Las Vegas pages, though NV Energy is the incumbent utility across Clark County as a matter of public record, and Switch has separately developed large solar generation, including the Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2 projects and the more recent Gigawatt Nevada solar-and-storage development, to support its stated 100 percent renewable energy claim across its Nevada campuses.

Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch's Core Campus, has helped establish Las Vegas as a significant secondary U.S. data center market outside the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs, drawing additional colocation and hyperscale investment from other operators over the past decade. Switch's original 2002 founding purchase, a former Enron-affiliated facility acquired at auction for 930,000 dollars, sat over a fiber-optic backbone corridor that shaped the campus's subsequent growth pattern along South Decatur Boulevard, West Capovilla Avenue, and Lindell Road, the streets along which most of Switch's larger, more recently documented Core Campus buildings, including Las Vegas 8, 9, and 10, are addressed.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility, Switch Las Vegas 11, is part of Switch Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, spanning locations including Las Vegas, Enterprise, and near McCarran. Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as CEO and chief engineer, and the company is headquartered in Las Vegas. Wikipedia coverage states that in 2002 Roy acquired a former Enron facility in Las Vegas at auction for 930,000 dollars, strategically located over a fiber optic backbone serving technology companies nationwide, which became the foundation of the Las Vegas Core Campus. That campus has grown to eleven operating data centers spanning over 2 million square feet, with plans to reach 2.3 million square feet across 12 buildings. Switch also operates the Citadel Campus in Storey County in Northern Nevada, a separate 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development announced in January 2015, and a Grand Rapids, Michigan Pyramid Campus, but those are distinct from this Las Vegas registry cluster. In December 2022 DigitalBridge and IFM Investors completed an 11 billion dollar acquisition, taking Switch private. Data center industry directories place Switch Las Vegas 11 at 7380 Lindell Road, Las Vegas, NV. Both datacenterHawk and DataCenterMap independently give this same address.  Switch own official locations page (fetched directly this session, https://www.switch.com/locations/) names five exascale campuses, the Citadel in Tahoe Reno, the Pyramid Campus in Grand Rapids, the Core Campus in Las Vegas, the Keep Campus in Atlanta, and the Rock Campus in Austin and Houston, but confirms no street address for any campus or building, directing visitors to a contact form instead. This registry rows address, where given below, therefore comes from data center industry aggregator directories, leads-only sources per this projects source hierarchy, not confirmed directly by the operator.

reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 11 is one of eleven data centers at the Las Vegas Core Campus, which spans over 2 million square feet across Clark County and has expansion plans to reach 2.3 million square feet.

The Las Vegas Core Campus represents consolidated compute infrastructure built on existing backbone connectivity. Switch acquired a former Enron facility in 2002 and developed it into a multi-building complex that now anchors the company's Western US operations. The campus's physical footprint and expansion trajectory reflect how data center operators cluster facilities in single regions to maximize fiber connectivity and shared infrastructure economies.

The data does not specify power capacity, power source, or grid connection details for this facility. It does not disclose the facility's current utilization, customer base, or workload composition. Switch itself publishes no building addresses on its official locations page, so the street address here derives from third-party data center directories rather than the operator's direct confirmation.

This facility sits within a larger portfolio that includes the Citadel Campus in Northern Nevada, acquired in 2015 as a 4 billion dollar, 1,000 plus acre development, and additional campuses in Atlanta, Austin, Houston, and Grand Rapids. The company transitioned to private ownership in December 2022 through an 11 billion dollar acquisition by DigitalBridge and IFM Investors.
